notes: Step 1 parts were correct and are unchanged.

The ADXL3xx breakout (catalogue type adxl335) is plugged into the breadboard with its six pins ST, Z, Y, X, GND, VDD in columns 4-9 of the top half as drawn. The image labels that half f-j, so it is bank 'b' in the catalogue naming, with the module in row j.

The exact breadboard holes for the wire ends are not fully visible in the image. Each wire's breadboard end is placed in row h of the same column as its breakout pin, so it shares a strip with that pin.
Wires: A0 to ST (blue), A1 to Z (yellow), A2 to Y (green), A3 to X (gray), A4 to GND (black), A5 to VDD (orange). This matches the tutorial's pin table and the schematic.
A4 is driven LOW as ground and A5 HIGH as 5 V in software, so the sensor is powered from the analog pins. The ADXL3xx pin VDD is the catalogue port VCC.
The tutorial notes that some ADXL3xx boards are 3.3 V only and 5 V could damage them. The circuit shown supplies about 5 V, following the tutorial's SparkFun breakout.
